title: rtsp ring robustness + telegram delivery wiring
author: jill
trigger: operator test 2026-09-08: vehicles driving by produced zero real-alert gate runs and zero telegram deliveries. Investigation found (a) two parallel RTSP readers per camera (boot-keyed by friendly name, lazy-keyed by prefix) causing registry key mismatch, (b) launchd plist carries a placeholder telegram bot token (7832687030:***) so the daemon cannot deliver even on real detections, (c) the reconnect loop does not trigger when a reader is stuck-in-demux (frames_decoded_total flat for hours). US-016 made logging and metrics visible; US-017 closes the loop on actual delivery.
background: US-016 completed log consolidation (/Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2/logs/daemon.log) and the /debug/rtsp endpoint (added during live troubleshooting 2026-09-08). The endpoint exposed the actual root cause of 'vehicles driving by but no alerts': registry keys do not match between boot (friendly name 'Outside Front Solar') and runtime (prefix 'OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR'). When /alert arrives and runs through the IP-fallback in listener/daemon.py, camera_id is rewritten to the prefix, and get_recent_frames(prefix) falls through CameraCaptureRegistry.get() lazy-init, which creates a SECOND reader under the prefix key. /debug/rtsp showed both keys live with frames, but the lazy one was the one the gate was reading from, and on first alert after boot it had not yet warmed up. Separately, the launchd plist at /Users/jill/Library/LaunchAgents/com.farm.surveillance.v2.plist hard-codes TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN as the literal string '7832687030:***' (operator note: real token lives in ~/.env at TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN). Daemon inherits the placeholder and telegram delivery fails end-to-end even when YOLOv8n fires. Third: previous daemon PID 1882 ran for hours with readers stuck in container.demux() without any reconnect log line, indicating the existing reconnect watchdog did not detect the wedge.
goal: Three structural fixes so /alert -> gate -> yolo -> telegram works on a real Reolink motion event: (a) single reader per camera, keyed by prefix; (b) daemon picks up the real telegram bot token from ~/.env at boot; (c) reader-wedge watchdog detects 'frames_decoded_total not advancing for N seconds' and forces a reconnect.
non_goals: Switching RTSP transport (tcp vs udp), changing the YOLO model, adding more cameras, restructuring the listener into separate processes, persistence/retention of motion frames beyond the existing /tmp ring buffer.
constraints: no private camera IPs, usernames, passwords, RTSP URLs, or telegram tokens may appear in scripts, configs, PRDs, or commit messages. Real values stay in camera-creds.env and ~/.env (gitignored).
Do not introduce infra/cameras.py or any code that requires camera-name translation. Pipeline already passes the prefix; the threshold JSON is keyed directly by prefix.
macOS objc AVFFrameReceiver collision warning remains acceptable and must not be silenced.
Bounce (kill + launchd respawn) requires explicit operator approval at the moment of bounce. The kill command and target PID must be stated before each bounce.
Stories commit individually; previous story must be done + committed + tree clean before next story is dispatched.
Numerical PRD sequence order is the implementation order. No dependency-resolved reorder.
Body of each story card stays <=2500 chars.
test_strategy: All ACs are concrete and verifiable via grep / pytest / curl / python3 -c. The pipeline is testable without real camera traffic by exercising the /alert route with synthetic payloads that resolve via real source IPs. Telegram delivery is verifiable end-to-end by inspecting the HTTP response from api.telegram.org on a test fixture.
shipping_definition: All stories marked done; pytest 116/116 (or higher) green; tree clean; daemon bounced once at the end of the PRD; manual real-traffic test (operator drives past a camera) results in a /alert log line followed by a motion_gate decision and a successful telegram sendPhoto HTTP 200.
files_out_of_scope: ~/.env (real telegram token lives here, gitignored, never read into repo)

stories.title: boot rtsp registry keyed by camera prefix (single reader per camera)
stories.card_body_fallback: CameraCaptureRegistry.start_all() currently iterates get_all_cameras() and registers each reader under the env-friendly key (e.g. 'Outside Front Solar'). The /alert handler in listener/daemon.py resolves camera_id to the prefix (e.g. 'OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR') via the IP-fallback loop. get_recent_frames(prefix) misses the boot key and the lazy CameraCaptureRegistry.get() creates a SECOND reader. /debug/rtsp shows both entries. Fix: in _boot_one, look up cam.get('prefix', camera_id) and use that as the registry key. Friendly name stays for human-readable log lines only. Single reader per camera, registry keys are all uppercase prefixes.
ac: AC1: grep -nE 'inst\._readers\[camera_id\]\s*=\s*reader' infra/frame_capture.py returns exactly one match and the right-hand side is keyed by the prefix (use cam.get('prefix', camera_id)).

AC2: python3 -c 'from infra.frame_capture import CameraCaptureRegistry; CameraCaptureRegistry.start_all(); print(sorted(CameraCaptureRegistry.stats_all().keys()))' prints six uppercase-prefix keys (FRONT, BACK, OUTSIDE_FRONT_GARAGE, OUTSIDE_FRONT_POWER, OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR, OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR) — no spaces, no duplicates.
AC4: After daemon bounce, /debug/rtsp returns exactly 6 camera entries (one per configured camera), all keyed by uppercase prefix.
stories.rationale: Live diagnostic on 2026-09-08 via /debug/rtsp (added in US-016 unblock) showed two readers per OFS camera: 'Outside Front Solar' (boot) and 'OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR' (lazy from /alert). Two parallel RTSP sockets per camera wastes bandwidth and decode CPU. The lazy path also means the first /alert after daemon bounce pays a 6+ second warmup penalty (which is what triggered the visible 'expected 4 frame_paths, got 0' errors during the 12:55 traffic burst). Single-key fix: register readers by prefix, matching the rest of the pipeline.

stories.title: load telegram bot token from ~/.env at daemon boot
stories.card_body_fallback: The launchd plist at /Users/jill/Library/LaunchAgents/com.farm.surveillance.v2.plist hard-codes TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN='7832687030:***' (placeholder). Real token is in ~/.env (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, 46 chars). Daemon inherits launchd env and gets the placeholder. Remove the TELEGRAM_* keys from the plist EnvironmentVariables dict. At listener/daemon.py main(), dotenv_values('~/.env') and merge into os.environ before CameraCaptureRegistry.start_all(). Log a one-line INFO 'Loaded N env vars from ~/.env' so operators can confirm.
ac: AC1: grep -nE 'TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN|TELEGRAM_HOME_CHAT_ID' /Users/jill/Library/LaunchAgents/com.farm.surveillance.v2.plist returns zero matches (plist is clean).
AC2: grep -nE 'dotenv_values|load_dotenv' listener/daemon.py returns >=1 match inside main().

AC3: After daemon bounce, tail logs/daemon.log shows 'Loaded N env vars from ~/.env' where N >= 2, and 'TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN length=46' (or similar length-revealing log line that does NOT print the secret value).
AC4: A test fixture in tests/ that calls daemon.main() with a mocked ~/.env asserts os.environ['TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN'] != '***' and len(token) >= 40.
stories.rationale: Without a real telegram token, even perfect YOLOv8n detections cannot deliver alerts. The placeholder was likely a deployment-time stub that was never replaced. Migrating the secret out of the plist (which is in a wider-readable location than ~/.env) is also better security posture. Merging env from ~/.env at startup keeps the daemon config-driven without leaking secrets into the repo.

stories.title: reader-wedge watchdog: detect flat frames_decoded_total and force reconnect
stories.card_body_fallback: CameraCaptureRegistry._reconnect_loop polls is_healthy() every 5s. is_healthy() returns False only when _healthy=False OR _last_frame_time is None OR (now - last_frame) > 5s. In the 2026-09-08 incident the previous daemon's readers were connected (container open, TCP socket ESTABLISHED) but stuck in container.demux() with no frames; _last_frame_time stayed at its boot value (None) which SHOULD have made is_healthy() return False, yet no 'Reader X unhealthy' log line appeared for hours. Add a second watchdog: every 30s, snapshot frames_decoded_total per reader. If a reader has been connected for >30s and the snapshot count has not increased since the last check, force-stop and replace the reader. Log 'Reader X stuck (no frames in 30s); reconnecting.' with the frames_decoded_total before and after.
ac: AC1: grep -nE 'frames_decoded_total' infra/frame_capture.py returns >=3 matches: the existing field declaration, the new snapshot in _reconnect_loop, and the comparison.
AC2: python3 -c 'from infra.frame_capture import CameraCaptureRegistry; print(hasattr(CameraCaptureRegistry, "_wedge_watchdog"))' prints True (or equivalent class method is present).

AC3: Unit test in tests/ simulates a wedge: stub a PersistentRTSPReader with frames_decoded_total that does not advance over two watchdog ticks; assert the watchdog calls reader.stop() and replaces it in the registry.
AC4: pytest tests/ -x --tb=short returns >= 117 passed (one new wedge-watchdog test added).
stories.rationale: Auto-recovery for the failure mode observed on 2026-09-08: a previous daemon ran for hours with readers wedged in container.demux() (TCP socket ESTABLISHED, _healthy=True after av.open(), _last_frame_time=None) and the existing is_healthy() chain did not log a reconnect. Without this watchdog, the operator must manually bounce the daemon to recover. The watchdog closes the class of failure rather than the instance.

verification_post_stories: git log shows three commits (one per story), each preceded by a clean tree.
Daemon bounced once after US-017c, PID recorded.
/debug/rtsp returns exactly 6 cameras, all keyed by uppercase prefix, ring sizes advancing.
logs/daemon.log shows 'Loaded N env vars from ~/.env' on boot.
Operator drives past FRONT or OUTSIDE_FRONT_SOLAR; /alert log line appears; motion_gate decision fires; telegram sendPhoto returns HTTP 200.
